clue.text: Hair stylists gamely facing the challenge of the freeze ?

definitions.text: Hair stylists gamely facing the challenge of the freeze

parts.words: Hair stylists gamely facing the challenge of the freeze
parts.note: two pictures in one word: what a hairdresser does with tongs, and the Scottish game of stones slid over ice

explanation.surface: Hairdressers bravely carry on working through a cold snap.
explanation.walkthrough: The game played on ice is one sense; the hairdresser's tongs give the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the setting of hair in ringlets and the winter sport of sliding granite stones across a frozen rink.

clue.text: In a cave the air is curiously fishy

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun: the delicacy that is fish roe

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are arranged in a curious, odd way

explanation.surface: The air in a cave smells strangely of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a' and 'the' and 'is' are links; 'curiously' rearranges CAVE and AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: This older spelling names salted sturgeon roe, a delicacy made from fish eggs.

clue.text: Passwords on the road

parts.note: words seen on new cars of the day, asking other drivers to pass because the engine is being driven gently

explanation.surface: Secret words are exchanged out on the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: A new car was once driven slowly for its first miles, with a notice in the rear window asking others to pass; those are the 'pass words'.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing a new engine through its first gentle miles was called this, and such cars carried a sign saying so.

clue.text: The nibs 'e broke !

indicators.note: the letters are broken apart and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A Cockney complains that he has broken his pen nibs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' rearranges NIBS and the dropped-aitch 'E; the Norwegian dramatist wore out many nibs writing his plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House wrote with pen and nib, and a man who writes much breaks them.

clue.text: Stars for the grizzled major

definitions.meaning: Ursa Major is Latin for the big she-bear, and a grizzly is a bear

explanation.surface: A grey-haired army officer is famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grizzled major' looks like an old officer; it is the grizzly bear and Ursa Major.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation Ursa Major, home of the Plough or Big Dipper, translates as the large bear.

clue.text: Indonesian home of my old Dutch?

definitions.text: Indonesian home of my old Dutch

parts.words: Indonesian home of my old Dutch
parts.note: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney for one's wife, but here it means the Dutch colonists of old, whose capital in Java this was

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks where in Indonesia his wife lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My old Dutch' is Cockney slang for 'my wife' (from duchess); read literally it is the Dutch of former times. The city is now Jakarta.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the colonial name the Netherlands gave to the Javanese port city that is now Jakarta.

clue.text: Devout first Earl of Norfolk ?

parts.note: the Norman Roger who first held the earldom has a surname that sounds like the oath 'by God', apt for a devout man

explanation.surface: We hear of the pious man who first held the Norfolk earldom.
explanation.walkthrough: Norfolk is an English county. The family name reads as 'by God', which is where 'Devout' comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger of that Norman family was created Earl of Norfolk in the twelfth century, the first of the title.

clue.text: It was eminently suitable for the dispatch' of the eminent

definitions.text: It was eminently suitable for the dispatch' of the eminent

parts.words: It was eminently suitable for the dispatch' of the eminent
parts.note: a raised place, an eminence, beside the Tower of London where noble traitors were beheaded

explanation.surface: Something was perfectly fitting for sending off important people.
explanation.walkthrough: An eminence is a hill, so 'eminently' points at high ground; the scaffold there executed famous prisoners from the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The rise beside the Tower of London was the public execution site for many noble prisoners.

clue.text: Small but severe affliction, man, to you and me

parts.note: vir is the Latin for man
us means you and me together

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend that a minor ailment can hit hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny infectious agent, too small for a light microscope, causes serious diseases.

clue.text: In a heat let one compete

definitions.text: In a heat let one compete

indicators.note: the letters vie with each other for new places, a jostling that rearranges them

explanation.surface: A race official says one runner may take part in a qualifying round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compete' rearranges HEAT LET; the whole clue is also the picture of a runner in a heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsman running in a qualifying heat is exactly what the word describes.

clue.text: Goddess visited by a far from ancient mariner

definitions.text: visited by a far from ancient mariner
definitions.meaning: the planet that the space probe Mariner 2 flew past in 1962, a very modern mariner

explanation.surface: A goddess receives a call from a young sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient mariner' calls up Coleridge's poem; the modern Mariner was an American space probe.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Roman goddess of love and the second planet from the sun, the first reached by a probe, carry this name.

clue.text: Rackrent accountant, sharp on valuation

parts.note: a sharp blade has an edge, and to have an edge is to be keen
worth is the value set on something

explanation.surface: A grasping landlord's bookkeeper is quick to price everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Maria Edgeworth wrote the novel Castle Rackrent, so she gave an account of Rackrent; 'accountant' is not a bookkeeper. 'on' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria of that surname was the Anglo-Irish novelist who narrated Castle Rackrent, so she is its teller of the tale.

clue.text: Ganymede's cousin and Edward are no longer friendly

parts.note: in As You Like It Rosalind disguises herself as Ganymede and her cousin Celia takes the name Aliena
Ted is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: A moon's relative and a man named Edward have fallen out.
explanation.walkthrough: Ganymede suggests Jupiter's moon, but it is Rosalind's disguise in Shakespeare's As You Like It; 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be estranged is to have been turned from warm feeling to coldness, as one-time friends become.

clue.text: Re-embrace a donkey that's a cat

indicators.note: the two letters of 're' hug the word for the animal between them

parts.note: taken as written
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone hugs a donkey again and finds it is a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Re-embrace' looks like one word meaning hug again; split it, 'embrace' puts ASS inside RE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rasse is a small civet of southern and eastern Asia, a cat-like carnivore.

clue.text: Poor Tom in a walled garden

indicators.note: the name sits inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A pitiable man is shut inside a walled garden.
explanation.walkthrough: In King Lear, Gloucester's son disguises himself as the mad beggar 'Poor Tom'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloucester's legitimate son in King Lear goes about as the beggar Tom o' Bedlam, calling himself Poor Tom.

clue.text: Riding his bay, the bowman

parts.note: Red Riding Hood and the robin redbreast both suggest red, as does the colour bay; the archer of Sherwood is meant

explanation.surface: An archer rides out on his reddish-brown horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riding' hints at Red Riding Hood, and a bay horse is reddish; the archer is the outlaw of Sherwood Forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest was famed above all as an archer.

clue.text: Develop an exact pile

annotationWithheld.why: 'Develop an exact pile (9)': EXACT PILE is the anagram fodder, but the only definition, 'Develop', must also be the only anagram indicator, a word doing two jobs

clue.text: Sailors leave wives unvisited although they have permits

definitions.text: Sailors leave wives unvisited although they have permits

parts.words: Sailors leave wives unvisited although they have permits
parts.note: a sailor with a wife in every port leaves them unvisited if he sails by those harbours

explanation.surface: Sailors with shore leave still fail to call on their wives.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, sailors 'pass ports' and miss their wives; the one word is the travel permits.
explanation.definitionFit: Official documents permitting travel abroad are what a traveller must carry.

clue.text: Speeches and where

definitions.meaning: formal talks given to an audience
the places where people live or letters go

explanation.surface: Someone asks what talks there are and where.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both formal speeches and the locations written on envelopes.

clue.text: They announced that Maud was in our wood among the lilies

definitions.text: They announced that Maud was in our wood among the lilies

parts.words: They announced that Maud was in our wood among the lilies
parts.note: in Tennyson's poem Maud the birds of the garden cry her name, and she is found in our wood gathering lilies

explanation.surface: Someone told the household that Maud was out picking lilies in the wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's Maud has the birds 'crying and calling' her name, and the line 'Where was Maud? in our wood' with woodland lilies.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds that sing, like those in Tennyson's poem calling Maud's name, are the creatures meant.

clue.text: Go under

parts.note: to sink or be overcome, as a business or a patient does

explanation.surface: Someone is told to sink.
explanation.definitionFit: To give way to an illness or a superior force is to be overcome by it.

clue.text: Noah's egg-spoon

parts.note: the eggs of all the creatures in the ark would call for an outsize spoon, a long-handled deep one

explanation.surface: We are shown the spoon Noah used at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: An ordinary egg-spoon is tiny; one for Noah, feeding a boatload of creatures, would be the biggest kitchen spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled spoon with a deep bowl, used for serving soup, is the largest of spoons.

clue.text: Where "even the weariest river winds somewhere safe to sea "

definitions.text: Where "even the weariest river winds somewhere safe to sea "

parts.words: Where "even the weariest river winds somewhere safe to sea "
parts.note: the line from Swinburne's The Garden of Proserpine; the place a river widens into the sea is meant

explanation.surface: We are asked where Swinburne's weary river finally reaches the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Swinburne's poem The Garden of Proserpine.
explanation.definitionFit: The tidal mouth of a river, where it meets the sea, is the place in question.

clue.text: Stop being dotty

parts.note: a stop is a punctuation mark, and this one consists of two dots

explanation.surface: Someone is told to quit acting crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like mad, but it means made of dots, and 'Stop' is the old word for a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark made of two dots, one above the other, was once called a stop.

clue.text: She ? O such a slip of a thing to get round one !

definitions.text: such a slip of a thing to get round one

parts.note: a lass is a girl, a she
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how small a girl is to manage a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip of a thing' looks like the slim girl; it is the slip noose of a cowboy's rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope with a running noose, thrown to catch cattle, slips tight around the animal.

clue.text: Am sorry about the measure taken to keep people away

indicators.note: the word for regret goes round the unit of length, so it is placed about it

parts.note: to repent is to be sorry, so 'I repent' means 'I am sorry'
an ell is an old measure of cloth, about 45 inches

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for the steps taken to keep visitors out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with this quality drives others off, as an insect spray does midges.

clue.text: Nabob's bob ?.

parts.note: a bob is a shilling, and a nabob is a man made rich in India, so his coin is the Indian one

explanation.surface: We are asked how a rich man wears his hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' is British slang for a shilling; a nabob is a European who made a fortune in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian unit of currency is the money such a returned fortune-hunter would count in.

clue.text: Chinese fruit of idyllic hills

indicators.note: the fruit is part of the words that follow, made of letters across their join

explanation.surface: A fruit from China grows on the slopes of a perfect landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the older spelling of the fruit usually written lychee.
explanation.definitionFit: The small sweet white-fleshed fruit with a rough red skin originates in southern China.

clue.text: Pop pop ?

parts.note: the first word as a verb, to make a cork go pop, and the second as a noun, the father, read as one who pulls the cork

explanation.surface: A child calls out to Grandpa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' is father and also the sound a cork makes; the one who pops the cork from a bottle is the person meant.
explanation.definitionFit: One who draws the cork or stopper from a bottle, making it go pop, opens it.

clue.text: One has a name for sunshine abroad

definitions.text: One has a name for sunshine abroad

parts.words: One has a name for sunshine abroad
parts.note: each Spanish coastal resort area has a name, and many speak of sun or gold

explanation.surface: Someone is famous for sunny foreign holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: Spanish holiday coasts all bear names: del Sol, Brava, Blanca and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for coast heads the names of sunny holiday shores such as del Sol and Brava.

clue.text: Smike's Yorkshire liberator

parts.note: in Nicholas Nickleby the bluff Yorkshire corn-factor John lets Smike out of the room at Dotheboys Hall where Squeers has locked him

explanation.surface: We are asked who freed a Dickens boy in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Smike is the ill-used boy at Squeers's Yorkshire school; the hearty John who frees him is not Nicholas himself. The checked O, D and E fit only this name.
explanation.definitionFit: John of that surname, the cheerful Yorkshireman in Nicholas Nickleby, releases the captive Smike from Squeers.

clue.text: Tumbles by the way in Lincs. ?

definitions.text: Tumbles by the way in Lincs.

parts.words: Tumbles by the way in Lincs.
parts.note: falls are spills, and 'spills by' said together gives the name of a market town in Lincolnshire

explanation.surface: A traveller keeps falling over on a Lincolnshire road.
explanation.walkthrough: The name sounds like 'spills by'; Lincs is short for Lincolnshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small market town in eastern Lincolnshire, at the edge of the Wolds.
